data.raw_text:
contrary to @AnnaMalindogUy's malicious insinuation that a foreign power has a privileged administrative exercise regime over 1,619 hectare of PH territory, perhaps she's not aware of existing arrangements between PH government and investors. such industrial relationships falls under Republic Act No. 7916 (The Special Economic Zone Act of 1995).

take Toyota PH. Toyota Motor Philippines (TMP) serves as the Administrator of the 82 hectare Toyota Special Economic Zone (TSEZ) in Santa Rosa, Laguna. as the zone developer and administrator, TMP has specific management responsibilities while remaining under the regulatory oversight of the Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA). TMP’s role within its private economic zone includes:

-TMP is responsible for the development, operation, and maintenance of utilities and infrastructure within the 82-hectare complex.

-locator supervision: the zone is home to various locators, typically export-oriented suppliers and partners, whose operations TMP helps coordinate.

-reporting and compliance: TMP holds regular update meetings with PEZA to report on export performance, investment updates, and operational challenges.

while PEZA is the government agency that officially issues environmental licenses and building permits, these processes for the Toyota SEZ are often coordinated through specific Zone Administrators to ensure efficiency. 

US and PH announced plans on April 16, 2026, to establish a 1,619 hectare within the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) and will be designated by the Philippines as an economic security zone (ESZ). located primarily in New Clark City, Tarlac. LEC will stretch through the central and northern parts of Luzon and encompass Metro Manila, Batangas province, the Clark airport and business hub in Pampanga, Subic Bay in Zambales, and other key urban and industrial zones. it will drive economic growth by improving connectivity between major ports and industrial hubs along the Luzon Economic Corridor. once operational, it will attract investments, create new opportunities for businesses, and most importantly, generate quality jobs that will benefit millions of Filipinos.

the hub is the first AI-native investment acceleration hub developed under the U.S. led Pax Silica initiative. the objective is to link economic activity with national security priorities by establishing a secure global technology supply chain. it serves as a golden node designed to build next gen manufacturing ecosystems for semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), infras and critical minerals. the hub aims to reduce global reliance on "coercive" supply chains and strengthen allied manufacturing network.

the US government, through the U.S. Trade and Development Agency (USTDA) and the Department of Transportation (DOTr), announced on June 26 last year, funding for technical assistance for the construction of the Subic-Clark-Manila-Batangas (SCMB) Railway, which is designed to link three major ports in Luzon and decongest traffic at the Port of Manila. the ESZ and the wider area of Luzon’s western corridor will be transformed into a more prosperous and interconnected region.

there are reports that the hub may operate under U.S. common law to entice and fast track investments.  located within the Luzon Economic Corridor, it leverages the PH mineral resources and skilled workforce to position the country as a regional AI and tech powerhouse. the zone aims to secure production for inputs critical to AI, semiconductors, electronics, and critical minerals, reducing global reliance on concentrated supply chains, particularly those controlled by China. it is designed as a purpose-built platform for "allied manufacturing," where activities are shaped by market demand and the comparative advantages of the Philippines. the ESZ can leverage the Philippines’ geographic centrality in the Indo-Pacific, its young and technically skilled workforce.
the hub will feature special visa lanes for foreign technical personnel, with a joint working group exploring reciprocal E-2 investor visa eligibility for Filipino nationals.

the Philippines became the 13th signatory to the Pax Silica declaration on April 16, 2026. other members include: founding/early members United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, India, Israel, Finland, Sweden, United Arab Emirates, and Qatar. Pax Silica is designed to align industrial development with economic competitiveness and security concerns across these member economies.
